title: Normalized finite inverse-image basis at one quotient exponent
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, a scheme $X$, and an object $W\to X$ of its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $R_X$ be the completed integral coefficient sheaf [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], let $L$ be an $R_X$-module sheaf, and fix a basis $e:L|_W\cong R_X|_W$ on the slice site [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Fix $n\ge0$, and put $A_{n,T}=(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^{n+1})_T$. Let $P=L[0]$, and let $H_n=W^*(A_{n,X}\otimes_{R_X}P)$ be the actual finite inverse-image complex, before restriction of scalars to the completed coefficients [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined]. For $U\to W$, write $V=(U\to W\to X)$ and let $T_U=(V\to W)$ be the corresponding slice object. Let $x_U\in P^0(V)$ be the image of $e^{-1}_{T_U}(1)$ under the inverse degree-zero single-complex identification. Let $\beta_{n,U}\in H_n^0(U)$ be the restriction, along the distinguished unit $U\to W\times_X V$, of the pullback-adjunction generator of $1\otimes x_U$. There is an isomorphism of complexes of $A_{n,W}$-modules $c_n:H_n\cong A_{n,W}[0]$ such that, for every $U$ and every $z\in A_{n,W}(U)$, its inverse in degree zero sends the single-complex representative of $z$ to $z\beta_{n,U}$. Only this fixed exponent is asserted; no compatibility with another exponent is assumed or concluded.

proof.text: Identify ordinary changeOfRings with changeOfRingsOfUniverses by the identity on sectionwise pure tensors and sheafification. Use the proved local scalar-extension basis construction extendedBasisIso to extend the degree-zero slice basis. Its coordinate map sends the pure tensor of one and the inverse basis vector to one. Transport through the prescribed object equality of unrestrictedIntegralReductionFunctor.

Use the concrete sliceFrom functor and the normalized constant-ring localization isomorphism. Its unit and counit equations give a sectionwise restriction/direct-image adjunction via pushforwardPushforwardAdj. Compare this adjunction to the actual coefficientProEtaleModuleAdjunction by uniqueness of left adjoints. The inverse comparison is the restricted actual pullback unit followed by restriction along the distinguished unit U to W times_X U, exactly the generator in the statement.

Transport the extended slice basis through sliceFrom and the constant-ring isomorphism, then compose with the actual pullback comparison. The inverse on one is the displayed basisGenerator: the constant-ring map preserves one, the scalar basis inverse sends one to the sheafified tensor of one and the inverse integral basis vector, and the comparison formula is the prescribed restriction of the pullback generator.

Apply the standard singleMapHomologicalComplex isomorphisms for reduction and pullback, and cancel the images of singleObjXSelf. The resulting complex isomorphism has the constructed module basis as its degree-zero map. Its inverse is linear, so its value at an arbitrary z is z times its value at one.

theorem finiteNormalizedBasis (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ c : finitePullback l E X W L n ≅ finiteRegular l E W.left n,
      ∀ (U : W.left.ProEt)
        (z : (integralCoefficientSheaf.{u, u} l E W.left n).obj.obj (op U)),
        (((finiteZero l E W.left n).inv ≫ c.inv.f 0).val.app (op U)) z =
          z • basisGenerator l E X W L e n U
